script.base: No spread or total is saved, so implied team totals are N/A and a blowout is not assumed. From weeks 1-3 only, SF is the side more likely to play ahead or in a competitive lead: DEN has allowed 5.30 YPC, 9 runs of 10+ and 11 passes of 20+ (117 yards), while SF has Christian McCaffrey 35/166 (4.74 YPC), Keon Black 25/107, George Kittle 16 targets/174 yards and Mike Evans 16/137 (questionable, ribs). DEN's run game is J.K. Dobbins 35/121 (3.46 YPC; game logs 36, 36, 49) into an SF rush defense at 3.79 YPC with only 3 runs of 10+. SF blitzes just 26% and DEN's EPA/dropback is -0.40 vs the blitz and +0.05 when not blitzed, but SF's edge is gutted (Nick Bosa out, Mykel Williams out, James Thompson Jr. out, Keion White questionable), so Denver can hang around with quicker throws rather than a pure rout. Base flow: SF run-lean if they lead, DEN pass-lean if they trail, moderate pace, no garbage-time assumption.
script.flip1: SF gets up big early, hands off to McCaffrey and Black (already 25 carries/107 yards), and Kittle, Evans and Brock Purdy yardage stall while Dobbins is abandoned. That flip kills a Kittle over and can add scramble rushes for Bo Nix.
script.flip2: The missing SF pass rush lets Nix stay clean, DEN leads or stays within a score, Dobbins keeps a full carry share, and SF has to throw (Kittle/Evans/Deebo Samuel) with Purdy scrambling into DEN's 38% blitz.

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone rates are not in the pack (no coverage charting). Saved location YPA only. SF defense: left 5.74 on 35 attempts, middle 7.29 on 14, right 6.45 on 53 — middle is the relative soft spot on a tiny sample; volume is to the right. DEN defense: left 7.78 on 37, middle 8.56 on 16, right 6.04 on 56 — middle and left bleed, right is the only respectable side. Against this DEN front the matchup is the hook/middle and the linebacker level, not a named outside corner.
matchup.pressure: SF blitz rate 26%; DEN EPA/dropback -0.40 when blitzed vs +0.05 when not. DEN blitz rate 38%; SF EPA/dropback +1.37 when blitzed vs +0.39 when not. SF wants Denver to blitz and should not fear it. Denver should not want extra rushers, but SF may not need to blitz much, and the four-man rush is the unit that just lost Bosa, Williams and Thompson. Pressure that does not get home protects deep shots and does not force the RB/TE checkdown spike.
matchup.bleeds: DEN run defense bleeds: 5.30 YPC allowed and 9 runs of 10+ in three games. DEN also bleeds explosives: 11 passes of 20+ for 117 yards, with middle YPA 8.56. SF does not bleed on the ground (3.79 YPC, 3 runs of 10+) and has allowed only 4 passes of 20+ for 108 yards. That SF explosive suppression is the counter to a Waddle or Sutton yardage over, and it is partly undone if the missing edge rushers are what created it.
matchup.overlap: The core overlap is Kittle, not a DEN wideout. He is tied for the lead SF receiving yardage (174 on 16 targets, 142 air yards, 8.9 air per target) and he attacks the layer DEN just lost (Tillman out) plus the explosive/middle bleed (11 passes of 20+, middle YPA 8.56) while his quarterback is outstanding vs the blitz DEN actually uses (38% blitz, SF 1.37 EPA/db). McCaffrey/Black into 5.30 YPC is the other overlap, but Black already has 25 of the backfield carries and McCaffrey's rush line is 65.5 vs a 55.3 per-game rush average (68, 23, 75), so the overlap does not clear a bettable rung. Waddle (247 air yards) into a defense that has allowed only 4 explosives is the wrong overlap, and the Bosa/Williams absences cut both ways.

data_check.notes: No projection, no sims, no Pinnacle, no coverage chart and no final inactives in the pack. model_p values are manual read estimates, not 3-sim probabilities, and must not be treated as clearing the +3 pt gate. Kittle is a strong scheme read and the yardage log disagrees: mean 58.0 on 12/80/82 is under 64.5, with a real floor game, so this is FLAG for the human, not a cut and not a sized bet. Treat anything that would have printed above 70% with suspicion; 0.60 is the ceiling used here on purpose. Nix under agrees with the 3/9/7 log, the 8/19 role and the SF edge outs; that lean is kept, not dropped. Dropped, not flagged: Dobbins under 59.5 (36/36/49 and SF 3.79 YPC look right, but Bosa, Williams, Thompson out and White questionable make the counter-case at least as strong as the read — step 10 drop). McCaffrey rush over 65.5 dropped because 11.7 carries times even DEN's 5.30 YPC allowed is about 62, under the rung, and Black has 25 carries. Purdy rush over 17.5 dropped as fluky 10.4 YPC on 9 carries despite 29/30/35. Waddle under 58 dropped: no price, one 138-yard game, and the missing SF edge rush cuts against a deep-ball under. No leg was cut solely by an average.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. Kittle repeated the 12-yard game because Evans played every snap, Denver stopped blitzing and bracketed the tight end after Tillman was out, and San Francisco led big enough to hand the ball to McCaffrey (35 carries, 166 yards already) and Black (25/107) so the routes died after halftime. Nix cleared 16.5 on two scrambles because that same DEN leak (5.30 YPC, 11 explosives) put Denver in a chase and he extended plays even with Bosa, Williams and Thompson on the sideline — QB rush yards do not need a healthy edge to happen once. The blowout flip is the shared kill and it is stronger than the base read only if SF is laying a number we do not have, which is why Kittle is flagged rather than sized and Nix stays a lean. We do not place the bet.
slip_story: One story, two legs, no TD: SF's offense can attack a DEN defense that bleeds explosives and just lost Tillman, while the gutted SF pass rush (Bosa, Williams, Thompson out) keeps Nix off scramble volume. That is not a shootout stack and not a favorite-runs-the-clock stack. Do not add McCaffrey rush over, Waddle over, or a total over — those need a different number or the opposite pressure script. A three-score SF lead breaks both legs; do not parlay them with anything that needs that blowout. Stop at these two.
